newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil products end firm in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil products end firm in thin trade.

text.p: NWE fuel oil prices lifted gently on Thursday as crude futures held up, but little real business was done with traders sceptical higher values will hold.
Fuel oil barge prices rose by $2 in the morning to trade at $92 fob ARA before settling back, with deals done at $90.50 and $88.50.
Bunker interest was stronger than usual and was being aggressively pursued by one refiner, dealers said.
The high sulphur cargo market was stable after its recent rise with utilities happy to wait for the product to lose the boost inherited from this week's futures rally.
"Numbers have gone up on the back of paper and nothing else," said one hesitant buyer. "There's a few dollars to come of those values yet."
Low sulphur barges were up on the back of short prompt supply. One refiner said he bought at $95 fob ARA on Tuesday and had been told figures were now higher.
"It will be difficult to find product now for less than $96 (fob ARA)," he said.

The low sulphur cargo market was thin, with values held down by weakness in the straight-run sector, where storage problems have released stocks of cheap material. Traders anticipated value creeping back as cargoes clear.
With oil product prices higher across the board in northern Europe since last week, two European refineries were confident enough of profit margins to restore cuts in plant throughputs.
Margins for a complex Rotterdam refinery have risen to $1.14 a barrel compared with 80 cents at the beginning of the month, according to Reuters price date using standard product yields.
